//: PROVENANCE AS A BUILD INPUT — SA §TS-12.3/§TS-12.4, SD §FE-10, SD Revision Log D8, as departed from under EV-16 (extended by stakeholder ruling OE-5, 2026-10-11) and OE-81. One record per safety_critical key PER LOCALE. `content_hash` is `sha256:` + lowercase hex SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the catalogue source string after Unicode NFC normalisation; `contentHash()` in src/review.ts is the one implementation and gate:safety-review-currency calls it. SINCE OE-5 NO HUMAN REVIEWS THIS COPY: every record is `ai_authored` (the model named in `authored_by`, the authorship ruling cited in `ruling` — OE-66 for el/ru, OE-67 for en), `status: "unreviewed_by_ruling"` with `review_ruling: "OE-5"`, and `reviewed_by`/`reviewed_at` null. That status means FINAL WITH NO REVIEW, by stakeholder ruling; it does not mean a review is pending. The gate's rule (T-258, T-259): for every safety_critical key and every enabled locale, FAIL unless the record exists; its hash matches the current source AND the hash pinned in the gate's own AUTHORED_CONTENT_PINNED; it is `ai_authored` under a ruling in tools/rulings.ts with that ruling's exact model as `authored_by`; it is `unreviewed_by_ruling` under OE-5; its `status` is not `signed_off` and no field whose name contains "review" other than `review_ruling` is non-null; it carries no field outside the nine a record defines; and its `note`, if present, is a string or null. The rulings are written in tools/rulings.ts, not here: a register that could grant its own authority would be measuring itself. Editing a safety string fails the gate until the same commit edits the record's hash and the gate's pin, which makes the edit visible in review of the diff; nothing here proves which model wrote the bytes. `pending_pipeline` is null: the dated waiver waited for a human review that OE-5 ruled out (T-259).

pipeline.//: THE PIPELINE AS DATA — T-049, SA §TS-12.4, as departed from under EV-16. Since stakeholder ruling OE-5 (2026-10-11; EV-16 extended) no human authors or reviews this copy: OE-66/OE-67 made an AI model its author and OE-5 dropped the DSL + deputy review. NO DATE IS IN FORCE HERE. T-259 deleted the deadline, the lead time, the latest external start, the external start and `blocked_on`, with their notes, because they measured the time left for a human engagement that the ruling abolished. `roles` and `stages` below still describe that human path: nobody is named, nothing is completed, and removing them is T-260's. The 360 px in-context check and the read-aloud check are NOT stages: under OE-82 they are automated gates (`automated_checks` below), and since T-264 gate:safety-review-currency refuses a record at the terminal status whose check is absent, stale or failed. `assignments` (the emergency-panel flag, the channel, the machine- and runtime-translation bans) is unchanged.

greek_authoring_safeguarding_practitione.what: Authors the English and Greek safety copy IN PARALLEL — not English first and Greek after. Must be a safeguarding practitioner working in Cyprus, because the copy encodes the Cyprus reporting pathway (112, 1466, 116 111, 199, Social Welfare Services) and not a UK one.

russian_translator_briefed.what: Professional translator, briefed on the safeguarding context BEFORE translating. The brief is a separate deliverable and a separate stage precisely because it is the step that gets skipped.

dsl.what: Designated Safeguarding Lead. Signs off PER LOCALE and is the only role whose name may appear in `reviewed_by`. The DSL and deputy BETWEEN THEM must cover English, Greek and Russian — a DSL who cannot read Russian cannot sign off Russian copy, and the deputy is how that is covered.
dsl.spec: PM §MVP-L5 AC7; SA §TS-12.4; SD Revision Log D8

dsl_deputy.what: Deputy DSL. Also permitted in `reviewed_by`. Exists in this roster because §MVP-L5 AC7 makes trilingual coverage a property of the PAIR, not of one person.

stages.what: English and Greek authored in parallel. NOT English-then-translate.
stages.output: Catalogue values for en and el; provenance `authored`.

stages.what: The safeguarding-context brief is delivered to and acknowledged by the translator, before any translation begins.
stages.output: A dated acknowledgement. Recorded here as the stage `completed_at`.

stages.what: Russian produced by the briefed human translator. Machine translation is prohibited at this tier (DV-11) and cannot produce a record in `entries` at all.

DSL review and sign-off, PER LOCALE. This is the step that writes `entries[<locale>][<key>]` with a real `reviewed_by` and `reviewed_at`, and it is the only step that can make gate:safety-review-currency pass.

automated_checks.what: SA §TS-12.4's read-aloud check, made by a gate under OE-82: every spoken safety string, in every enabled locale and every plural form, is synthesised with espeak-ng and checked for speakable tokens, sentence length and duration; the record binds each pair's content_hash. Which keys it applies to is pinned in tools/automated-checks.ts (READ_ALOUD_KEYS_PINNED), not here. Nothing it synthesises ships (DV-7).

SA §TS-12.4's in-context check, made by a gate under OE-82: every shown safety string is rendered in the running product at a pinned 360 px Android viewport in every enabled locale, and refused if it is not visible, differs from the catalogue, clips, truncates, overflows or is a tap target under 44x44. Which keys it applies to is pinned in tools/automated-checks.ts (RENDER_KEYS_PINNED); a key whose surface does not exist yet is listed in AWAITING_SURFACE against the ticket that builds it, and that list must be empty for production readiness.

safety.emergency.address_prompt.channel_note: The user reads this ALOUD to a 112 operator while an emergency is in progress. It must survive being spoken by a frightened person, not merely read on a screen — SA §TS-12.4 read-aloud pass.

en.why: Source authorship. SA §TS-12.4: English and Greek are authored IN PARALLEL by the safeguarding author.

el.why: MUST be natively authored, never translated from English. PM §MVP-L4 AC4 and §MVP-S7 AC1 both require Greek AUTHORSHIP. A Greek translation of an English safety string is a different artefact from a Greek safety string and this field is where the difference is enforced rather than hoped for.

ru.why: Professional translator BRIEFED ON THE SAFEGUARDING CONTEXT (PM §MVP-L4 AC4). SA §TS-12.4: a translator who does not know a string is an escalation message will produce a grammatically perfect, operationally useless one. Machine translation is prohibited outright at this tier (DV-11) and the brief is a required, separately-recorded stage.

session.checkins_missed.channel_note: UNDETERMINED, and fail-closed on purpose. This is an escalation-ladder message, and DV-7 adds an automated VOICE rung with pre-recorded audio per locale (SA §INT-5r). Whether this key is rendered on that rung is T-105/T-107’s determination, not this ticket’s. A record may not be signed off while its channel is undetermined, because the read-aloud pass would silently not apply.
